hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no signal, so a conv on edge 1->3 contributes nothing.
Edge 2 carries node 1's output, which is empty when edge 0 is none, so the edit is useless.
Replacing none with a conv on the direct input-to-output edge gives a bigger gain than replacing another op.
Edge 0 being none cuts off node 1 entirely, so filling it with a conv recovers much more accuracy.
Replacing none on a main edge into the output with a conv gives a large gain relative to replacing other ops.
Replacing none with a conv adds a new learnable path, a larger gain than swapping one op for another.
A skip on the 0->3 edge adds a residual path, which helps much more over none than over a conv.
Edge 1 being none leaves node 2 with less input, so a conv on edge 5 has little to process.
Swapping a 3x3 conv for pooling on the direct edge loses far more than replacing other ops with pooling.
Adding a conv where the edge was none gives a bigger gain than replacing other ops.
